Subject: Post-call: Ledgerly integration scope & JSON validation / retry strategy

Hi Elena / Ledgerly team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to line up goals and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of asks from Ledgerly:
- Structured transaction enrichment API that returns a strict JSON blob per record (see the sample fields in attached ledgerly-schema-v1.json).
- High reliability for batch inference (low failure rate) and deterministic schema adherence for downstream ingestion.
- Auth requirement: customer-managed API keys with optional mTLS for production.
- Routing: US region priority, fall back to dedicated pool, SLO target 95th perc latency < 250ms for typical 512-token calls.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer batching and prefix caching to keep per-transaction token cost constrained.

Proposed immediate steps (action owners in parentheses):
1) Redwood to supply a concrete validation + retry pattern and a minimal SDK snippet showing schema validation & idempotency patterns (Rishi) — due Mon 2/29.
2) Ledgerly to confirm schema fields and required/optional flags (Elena) — due Fri 2/27.
3) Tech sync to finalize auth approach (API key vs mTLS) and routing rules (all) — propose Tue 3/2 at 10am PT.

Attachments: ledgerly-schema-v1.json (sample schema), Redwood playbook excerpt (redwood-structured-output-playbook.pdf).

Thanks Naomi — great summary. Attaching a short tech note and an example SDK pattern below. Main recommendations for structured-output reliability: 

1) Constrained decoding + schema enforcement (server-side + client-side):
   - We will compile Ledgerly's schema into a strict JSON Schema (attached) and enforce at generation time using constrained decoding: model constrained by prompt framing + sampling params (temperature=0.0, top_k=1 when deterministic fields) and token/sequence length guards.
   - Runtime validator will run post-generation with 2 layers: quick structural check (fast JSON Schema validate) then soft checks (value ranges, enumerations). Non-conforming outputs will trigger either automated repair (retry with an explicit "sanitize" instruction) or return a diagnostic payload.

2) Retry patterns & idempotency:
   - For transient infra/model errors (5xx/timeouts) use exponential backoff with jitter: initial 250ms, *2, cap 4s, 3 retries.
   - For schema-mismatch responses: attempt a single automated constrained-retry with a stricter prompt + schema hint (idempotent) and include an idempotency key so Ledgerly can dedupe in their pipeline. If still invalid, fail fast with a structured error object (error_code, field_errors, attempt_trace).

3) SDK suggestions (pseudo-JS):
   - Auth: support API key header + optional client cert config.
   - Route selection: SDK will try region endpoint (us.redwood.ai) then fall back to dedicated://<pool> when host returns 429 or capacity signals.
   - Validation helper: redwood.validateSchema(response, 'ledgerly-schema-v1'); redwood.retryWithBackoff(fn, {retries:3, backoffMs:250});

4) Operational recommendations:
   - Instrument token-level error rate and schema-failure rate per route/model.
   - Canary traffic on structured-output changes (5% -> 25% -> 100%).

I’ve attached a one-page playbook PDF and the schema (ledgerly-schema-v1.json). If Ledgerly wants, I can prepare a minimal runnable SDK example (node + curl) for the Tue 3/2 sync.

–Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-structured-output-playbook.pdf, ledgerly-schema-v1.json

Hi Naomi / Rishi,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side before the Tue sync: 

1) Auth: production must use our KMS-backed mTLS certs for the ingestion endpoint. API keys can be used for initial testing but not for prod.
2) Schema: we’ve reviewed ledgerly-schema-v1.json and will mark two fields optional (merchant_notes, geo_subregion) — updated file attached to this reply.
3) Failure semantics: we prefer a conservative approach — if a response fails schema validation after the automated retry, return the structured error object and put the record into our "hold-for-manual" queue. No silent repair unless the repair is an unambiguous structural fix (e.g., stray trailing comma).

We confirm the Tue 3/2 10am PT sync. Also can you include the minimal node SDK example and a short runbook for operations? That will help our infra team evaluate mTLS setup.

Thanks,
Elena Torres

elena@ledgerly.com
